set.approach: Most parties start at the Andrews Creek trailhead (trail 504) at the edge of the Pasayten Wilderness. Follow the valley about four miles to the usual first camp in the burned section, cross Andrews Pass, then join the Boundary Trail to Upper Cathedral Lake; the whole trip is roughly 17 miles with about 4,800 ft of gain. Camp near the lake, which fills a boulder-strewn basin right under the north face of Amphitheater Mountain. Looking up from the shore, the Middle Finger Buttress is the one to the right of the Ka'aba Buttress; walk around the shore and scramble about 15 minutes up to the base of Middle Finger Buttress, where the route starts on the face directly above the lake.

review.notes: Trailhead, burned valley camp, Andrews Pass, Boundary Trail, ~17 mi/4,800 ft and the lake-side buttress layout from the two trip reports; the 15-minute scramble to the buttress base comes from the sibling Left Side approach in the catalog, not re-confirmed on the web.

set.approach: Start at the Big Four Ice Caves trailhead on the Mountain Loop Highway (a Northwest Forest Pass is needed for parking). The Ice Caves trail is an easy, mostly boardwalk and paved path of about 1.1 miles each way with roughly 220 ft of gain, passing the old hotel site at the picnic area, crossing the South Fork Stillaguamish on a bridge, and opening into a meadow below the north side of the mountain. Leave the trail at the end and head across the open basin toward the foot of the north-side ridge you are climbing.

review.notes: Trail length, gain, bridge, picnic area and pass requirement from the trail page; that this route starts from the Ice Caves viewpoint comes from the existing catalog text. Descent not written: no source found.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the southwest summit (about 9,320 ft) after merging with the upper Soviet Route, and the way down is the same as for that route. Follow the crest northeast to the West Peak, which takes close to two hours because the gendarmes are mostly bypassed on third and fourth class ledges with one short rappel. From the West Peak, downclimb talus on the northwest side to a band of steep slabs, then make two rappels of about 200 ft each; anchors are improvised from natural features, so carry cord and a few nuts or pitons. Below the slabs, downclimb to the talus, traverse beneath the buttress to the North Star-Bonanza col, and expect to arrive at camp very late after a full day. The steep south face descent over glaciers and cliffs is the alternative, but it is long and committing.

review.notes: Oregonian joins the Soviet Route for its last 600 ft to the SW summit (AAC 2014); the Soviet descent via West Peak, two 200 ft rappels and talus to the col from the 2012 repeat trip report. Nobody has described an Oregonian-specific descent, so it is inferred from the shared finish.

set.descent_text: This is a long ridge traverse that links Needle Peak, Dark Peak and the crest to Bonanza, so there is no easy retreat once committed; the way down is from the Bonanza summit ridge by the Mary Green Glacier route. Expect to descend that glacier in the evening after a full day on the crest, with heavy crevassing that calls for roped glacier travel and care in the dark. Continue down to the Holden Pass high camp and then out the Holden Lake trail to Holden Village. Do not start this traverse in unsettled weather, since backtracking along the crest is the only alternative.

review.notes: The 2007 AAJ report supports the Needle-Dark-Bonanza traverse, retreat only by backtracking and the crevassed Mary Greene Glacier descent in the evening; Holden Pass camp and Holden Lake trail out are from the catalog's standard-route entry.
